findings.failure_scenario: MainActivity.onCreate calls Utils.isFirstAppStart(this) on every launch. On a fresh install, KEY_SHARED_PREFERENCES_HISTORIES has never been written, so SettingsUtils.readStringFromSharedPreferences(ctx, key) (the 2-arg overload at SettingsUtils.java:61-64) returns getString(key, null) = null, and null.isEmpty() throws NPE before WelcomeActivity can start. Every subsequent launch crashes identically because the crash prevents any code path from writing the key. The same crash hits existing users whose KEY_SHARED_PREFERENCES_FIRST_TIME flag was never set to false (users who already had clicked stories stored when that flag was introduced), so the app becomes completely unusable. The old code read an int set via readIntSetFromSharedPreferences, which never returns null.
findings.summary: isFirstAppStart dereferences a possibly-null SharedPreferences string: the new histories key returns null when absent, and .isEmpty() throws NullPointerException at app startup.

findings.failure_scenario: Running ./gradlew assembleDebug fails: UtilsKt.kt:47 `for (i in 0..<size)` is parsed by the 1.8.0 compiler as the @ExperimentalStdlibApi rangeUntil operator, and using it without @OptIn(ExperimentalStdlibApi::class) is a compile error ('this declaration is experimental...'). The diff bumped only the root buildscript classpath to kotlin-gradle-plugin 2.1.21 (build.gradle:10), but app/build.gradle requests the plugin versionlessly via the plugins {} DSL, which inherits 1.8.0 from the unchanged root `plugins { id 'org.jetbrains.kotlin.android' version '1.8.0' apply false }` (build.gradle:16) — the buildscript classpath bump is not consulted, so the intended 2.1.21 upgrade never reaches the module. At best the version bump is dead configuration; at worst (the standard plugins-DSL resolution) the build breaks.
findings.summary: New Kotlin code uses the `0..<size` range-until operator (stable only in Kotlin 1.9+), but the Kotlin plugin actually applied to the app module is still 1.8.0, so compilation fails.

findings.failure_scenario: A user upgrading from the previous version has N read story ids stored under the old SharedPreferences key KEY_SHARED_PREFERENCES_CLICKED_IDS (constant deleted from Utils.java). The new code only reads the brand-new KEY_SHARED_PREFERENCES_HISTORIES string, which is empty for them, so every previously read story renders as unread, 'hide read stories' (hideClicked) stops filtering, and the History tab is empty. The old data is never imported or cleaned up — the read-state data is lost with no code path to recover it.
findings.summary: No migration from the removed KEY_SHARED_PREFERENCES_CLICKED_IDS storage: all previously clicked story ids are silently orphaned on upgrade, resetting every user's read state.

findings.failure_scenario: In the onLongClick listener, `History h = HistoriesUtils.INSTANCE.getHistorybyId(story.id);` is computed and immediately discarded (no later reference in the method); only the History import and an extra blank line remain. This is leftover scaffolding from the change — a maintainability cost (misleading read that implies the fetched timestamp is used, plus a linear scan per long-press) with no behavioral benefit; no runtime failure.
findings.summary: Dead code: the local variable `h` fetched via HistoriesUtils.INSTANCE.getHistorybyId(story.id) in the long-press handler is never used.
